name: Pulmonary Hypertension with Unclear Multifactorial Mechanism
aliases: Pulmonary Hypertension of Unclear Multifactorial Origin

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2015 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Presence of multifactorial or unclear underlying causes not fitting other pulmonary hypertension groups
Exclusion of pulmonary arterial hypertension (Group 1), left heart disease (Group 2), lung diseases/hypoxia (Group 3), and chronic thromboembolic PH (Group 4)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hemodynamic confirmation by right heart catheterization with mPAP ≥ 25 mmHg and PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg, exclusion of other defined causes of pulmonary hypertension, and identification of unclear or multifactorial etiology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on invasive hemodynamic measurements and exclusion of other causes; multifactorial mechanisms may include hematologic, systemic, metabolic, or other disorders.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive shortness of breath on exertion
Palpable precordial impulse due to right ventricular hypertrophy
searchTerms: visible heart lift on right side

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
common.notes: Generalized tiredness and reduced exercise tolerance
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.notes: Swelling of lower extremities due to right heart failure
Transient loss or near loss of consciousness
searchTerms: fainting or near fainting with activity

occasional.notes: Coughing up blood due to pulmonary vessel rupture
Enlarged liver secondary to right heart failure

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal pain due to congestive hepatopathy
searchTerms: abdominal discomfort due to liver swelling

rare.notes: Bluish discoloration of skin and mucous membranes
Digital clubbing due to chronic hypoxia

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
Mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: Echocardiography showing right ventricular hypertrophy and elevated pulmonary artery pressures
Chest X-ray with enlarged pulmonary arteries and right heart enlargement
CT pulmonary angiography excluding thromboembolic disease
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; multifactorial etiology
other: Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mean pulmonary artery pressure
Ventilation-perfusion scan to exclude chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension

distinguishingFeatures: Known genetic mutations or idiopathic origin
Characteristic perfusion defects on ventilation-perfusion scan

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure such as severe peripheral edema or ascites
references: Galiè N, Humbert M, Vachiery JL, et al. 2015 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2016;37(1):67-119.
Simonneau G, Montani D, Celermajer DS, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019;53(1):1801913.
Orphanet: Pulmonary hypertension with unclear multifactorial mechanism (ORPHA:275844)
